text.title: User Research at Scale Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding the User Research at Scale methodology. Every rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale, plus the universal skip-this-methodology gate.

rule.statement: Coding MUST apply a frozen codebook; novel themes go to a proposed_codes overflow channel for weekly review, never auto-applied. Lock the codebook before collection; version it (v1.0.0) and bump only with documented diffs; use a separate proposed_codes overflow channel instead of modifying the codebook mid-study.
rule.rationale: Auto-extending the codebook produces theme drift; the overflow channel preserves novelty without polluting the book. Theme drift across batches is the #1 AI coding failure mode. A frozen codebook with a version + proposed_codes channel surfaces emergent themes for human review without corrupting the existing taxonomy. The theme-coder prompt that enforces this is in `content/05-examples.xml`.

rule.statement: Any published finding MUST be supported by >=50 coded observations across >=10 sessions and >=2 segments.
rule.rationale: Below the floor, findings reflect noise or coding bias.

rule.statement: Findings MUST pass a human-in-the-loop review before publish; no auto-publish. Add a "draft/published" gate on every finding — dashboards auto-update faster than humans can vet.
rule.rationale: AI coding mistakes propagate; HITL catches them. Unvetted AI findings reaching a product meeting without a human review can redirect roadmap decisions based on hallucinated patterns.

rule.statement: Interview transcripts and any PII MUST be processed through ZDR-eligible LLM endpoints only.
rule.rationale: Privacy + DSA compliance; non-ZDR retention is a legal liability.

rule.statement: Transcripts MUST be speaker-attributed; interviewer turns are stripped before coding.
rule.rationale: Coding interviewer prompts as user statements inflates false themes.

rule.statement: All writes to Dovetail/Notion/CRM via API MUST use idempotency keys (hash of source + date).
Run theme-coder and bias-auditor in parallel; gate report-writer on a researcher human-in-loop checkpoint at step 8.
rule.rationale: AI synthesis can proceed while bias audit runs — they are independent. But publishing without a human checkpoint after synthesis lets AI-invented "insights" reach stakeholders without review.

rule.statement: Assign Haiku to mechanical tasks (panel-sampler, protocol-runner, transcript-cleaner, dashboard-publisher); Sonnet to structured synthesis (theme-coder, quote-curator, bias-auditor); Opus to cross-segment pattern mining and executive synthesis.
rule.rationale: This assignment minimizes cost while matching model capability to task complexity. Inverting it — Opus on transcript cleaning, Haiku on pattern mining — either burns tokens or degrades quality. The subagent table is in `content/04-procedure.xml`.

rule.statement: Sample 10% of AI-coded segments for human re-coding every batch; track inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa >= 0.7) and recalibrate when it drops below threshold.
rule.rationale: AI coding accuracy drifts as transcripts vary in quality and subject matter. Kappa tracking catches drift before it contaminates an entire study's findings.

rule.statement: Gate on Whisper confidence score >= 0.6 per transcript before coding — low-quality audio produces confident-but-wrong text that the coder cannot distinguish from accurate transcription.
rule.rationale: Downstream coding errors from bad transcription are undetectable at the finding layer. The confidence gate catches the problem at the source.

rule.statement: Cache full transcripts in the LLM context using prompt caching when coding hundreds of quotes against the same codebook — the savings are substantial at scale.
rule.rationale: Repeated codebook context is identical across all transcript coding calls. Prompt caching eliminates the redundant token cost of loading the codebook on every call.

rule.statement: Publish disconfirming quotes alongside confirming ones — outliers are signal, not noise.
rule.rationale: LLM summarization compresses outliers. The most valuable insights often come from the user who had the unexpected reaction. Requiring outlier inclusion in the quote bank prevents systematic suppression.

rule.statement: Stratify panels by behavior (active/lapsed/new), not just demographics — demographic-only sampling hides usage truth.
rule.rationale: Demographic similarity does not predict usage similarity. Active and churned users of the same age have opposite perspectives on the product's value.

rule.statement: Triangulate every finding with AI sentiment + behavioral analytics + verbatim quote — never report from one source alone.
rule.rationale: Single-source findings have low reliability at scale. Three-source triangulation with confidence tiers (high >= 3 types, medium = 2, low = 1) enables stakeholders to calibrate trust. Complements n-fifty-per-finding: that rule sets the observation floor, this one the source-type floor.

rule.statement: Redact PII with Presidio before any external LLM call; confirm that platform recordings have consented to AI processing before feeding into the pipeline.
rule.rationale: Sending raw PII to a non-zero-retention LLM endpoint violates GDPR and platform ToS. Presidio redaction runs locally before any external call. Consent flags must be read by the transcript-cleaner before quoting. Complements zdr-only-for-pii: redaction happens before the ZDR endpoint is even reached.

rule.statement: Never present synthetic users or AI-generated personas as real research findings.
rule.rationale: Synthetic personas leak training-data clichés and introduce systematic bias toward the modal user in the training set. They are planning tools, not research evidence.

rule.statement: Apply this methodology only if all entries in `## Applies If` hold and none of `## Skip If` triggers; otherwise abort and route to the correct methodology.

rationale.source: F-066 spec — decision tree minimum form

rule.rationale: A misrouted methodology produces wrong-shape output; the explicit skip rule is the universal default branch from the decision tree.
